sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for install prompt
sections.what: Brings in React state, icons, a button, and the notification helper used to confirm installation.
sections.why: The install prompt needs its look, a way to show a message, and state to track it.

sections.name: PWAHandler (part 1)
sections.title: Background setup for app install
sections.what: On first load, registers the offline helper file named sw.js so the app can work offline. It also listens for the browser's install offer and saves it. After five seconds, it shows the install bar, but only if the user has not already dismissed it. When installation completes, it hides the bar and shows a confirmation message.
sections.why: Lets users install Maate to their home screen and use it offline. The five second delay avoids interrupting the first moments of a visit. Reason for the delay is only partly stated in the code comment.
sections.watch_out: The event listeners are added but never removed, so they can stack up if the component is mounted again. The service worker only registers after the page load event, so it may register late on slow connections.

sections.name: PWAHandler: if
sections.title: Install bar with install and later buttons
sections.what: Shows a bottom card asking the user to install the app. Add to Home Screen starts the browser's install prompt, then remembers the choice. Later and the close icon hide the bar and also remember the choice so it does not return.
sections.why: Gives a clear, one time choice about installing without repeating the offer.
sections.watch_out: The dismiss memory lives in local browser storage, so clearing site data will bring the prompt back. The Add to Home Screen handler does not check whether the prompt call fails.

summary: Registers the offline support file and shows a bottom banner inviting the user to install Maate on their home screen.
purpose: Helps the patient install the app and turns on offline support.
why: Header says registration and install experience. The stored flag suggests the banner is not shown again after the user has responded, but the code does not state this.
how: On load, registers the service worker from sw.js. Listens for the browser's install offer and keeps it. After five seconds, shows the banner if the user has not answered before. The Add to Home Screen button opens the browser's install prompt. Both that button and Later save a flag in local storage. A success message shows when the app is installed.
inputs: Browser events, the browser's install offer, and the saved flag in local storage.
outputs: The install banner, a service worker registration, a success message, and the saved flag.
risks: Listeners are added each time the component mounts and never removed, so they can pile up. Service worker and install errors are only written to the console, so the user sees nothing when they fail.
debug: If the banner never shows, check that the browser offered an install prompt and that the maate_install_prompt flag is not already set in local storage. If offline support fails, check that sw.js exists and read the browser console.
